and secure remote access.
# dsh-deeppilot
**English** | 简体中文

The open-source DSH companion plugin for **DeepPilot**, a native iPhone client
for using DeepSeek Ha

rness remotely. It connects the app directly to the DSH
Host on your own computer and does not repla
ce or modify the DSH Web UI.

> DeepPilot is currently in TestFlight review. The invitation link will accept
> testers after Apple
approves the build.
Join the DeepPilot TestFlight
## What you get

- Browse projects, sessions, history, and live agent output from iPhone.
- Stream assistant text and

reasoning while viewing a session; reconnects recover
the durable history rather than treating part

ial output as a completed answer.
- Export a full ZIP log archive, or share the conversation body as

Markdown when
the Host provides that optional route.
- Check plugin updates from the app and instal

l an explicitly confirmed compatible
version. The Host handles hot replacement and rollback; without

hot reload the
app reports that a DSH restart is required.
- Send prompts, switch models, create se

ssions, and answer approvals/questions.
- Pair with a five-minute single-use code and a per-device P

-256 key; physical
iPhones keep the private key in Secure Enclave.
- Connect over the LAN (TLS with

a Host-issued certificate pinned during
pairing) or the optional embedded Tailscale Funnel.
- Receiv

e live notifications and optional APNs notifications while offline.
- Local web preview: open a `htt

p://127.0.0.1:<port>` or `localhost:<port>`
link from the conversation (a design canvas or dev serve

r the agent started)
inside the app, with its live reload intact.
- Quiet scheduled runs (DSH 0.2.2+

): write a rule into a scheduled task's
prompt, such as "if everything is normal, don't notify me".

The agent can
then skip that run's "task completed" notification with the
`deeppilot_skip_completion

_notice` tool. Approvals, questions and errors
still notify, and tasks without such a rule notify on

every run as before.
- Self-update hint: the settings page footer shows the installed plugin
versio

n, with an inline "new version" link to the matching GitHub
release when one exists (background chec

k, stable releases only, no
third-party dependency).
## Install from npm

This source checkout targets Node.js 22+ and DSH hosts inside the rolling
compatibility range `>=0.2

.1-rc.5 <0.3.0-0` with a `web` profile. The lower
bound is the newest audited `rc` release at decisi

on time — npm `latest` and
`next` both point at `0.2.1-rc.5` — and every later `0.2.x` release is ad

mitted
automatically, including the `alpha` channel release `0.2.2-alpha.2` and later
alphas, later

rc releases, and `0.2.x` GA. `0.3.0` and its prereleases stay
refused until a fresh audit. DSH check

s a plugin's declared requirements before
composing a profile, on every start rather than only on in

stall, so a host
outside the range refuses to activate this plugin. From DSH `0.2.1-alpha.4` on,
tha

t check reads `engines.dsh` and ignores `peerDependencies`; older hosts know
only the peer range, so

both declare the identical range. The package includes
Funnel helpers for macOS, Linux, and Windows

on amd64/arm64; trusted-LAN mode
does not require the helper. The helper is built with Go 1.27, whi

ch requires
**macOS 13 Ventura or later**: on macOS 12 and earlier, Funnel mode cannot
start, while
trusted-LAN mode keeps working.

The current working tree declares that range in `engines.dsh` and
`peerDependencies` and is built/ty

pechecked against `0.2.1-rc.5`. A previously
published plugin package may still carry its own older

compatibility
declaration until a release is made from this tree.

After DSH restarts, open **Settings → DeepPilot**, turn on **Allow phone connections**,
and click **
Add phone** beside **Paired devices**, then scan the QR code in the app. The same panel also shows o

ne copyable piece of pairing info (address, single-use code and
certificate fingerprint) that can be

pasted into the app in one step — useful for

## Connection and privacy

Conversation traffic travels directly between the iPhone and your DSH Host and
is always encrypted:

the LAN listener on port `3098` serves TLS with a
self-signed certificate whose fingerprint the app

receives during pairing, and
Funnel mode uses Tailscale-issued certificates. The app refuses plain `

ws://`.
Both the LAN listener and optional Funnel mode expose only the DeepPilot
connection, one-tim
e pairing, and health endpoints, not the complete DSH Web UI.

Local web preview forwards raw bytes over a separate authenticated connection
to a loopback port on

this computer. A port is reachable only after it has
appeared in that session's messages; the plugin

's own ports and the DSH Web
default port `3080` are always refused, and only `http` loopback links

with an
explicit port qualify. The settings page's **Local web preview** switch (on by
default) turn
s it off for every paired phone; open streams close at once.

The DeepPilot settings page exposes **Connections per public source**. It
defaults to `8`, accepts `

1`–`16`, and briefly restarts the Funnel helper when
changed, so connected remote clients reconnect

once (its exact section may
move between DSH versions; go by the settings page's current layout). Th

e
device list also supports a custom name for each paired device. Names are
stored in the host regis

try and survive iPhone reconnects or changes to the
system-reported name; saving an empty value rest

ores the iPhone-reported
default.

Each device's **More actions** control contains its fingerprint, rename action,
and deletion action;

deletion still requires confirmation. Connection options,
connection help, diagnostic tools, and sy

stem information start collapsed.
Desktop secondary buttons are 28px high; custom action touch targe

ts remain at
least 44px. **Add phone** uses DSH's built-in small outlined `Button`; all
toggles use

its `Switch`. Native controls keep the host's appearance and sizing.
See settings UI and validation.

The settings page's **Diagnostic tools** group has a `debug` toggle.
Turning it on prints per-frame

and push diagnostics to the DSH host's terminal
[该节后续省略]
## Compatibility

See COMPATIBILITY.md for the tested baseline and current
limitations. DSH is still evolving; include

exact DSH and plugin versions when
reporting an issue.
